transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
Lately I keep thinking my clients would be better off if I just weren’t here. Those thoughts about not wanting to wake up are starting to really scare me, which is why I'm here.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about not wanting to wake up and feeling like your clients would be better off without you?
All of this has been weighing on me for about a month now. It really started after a very stressful stretch at the clinic with some difficult cases and a tense disagreement with my supervisor.
Have you noticed a decrease in interest or pleasure in activities you normally enjoy over the past month, or is it more about these specific thoughts and feelings of being a burden?

It’s definitely both. I've completely lost interest in things I used to love, like playing my guitar or hanging out with friends, and now it just feels like I'm going through the motions. At the same time, I'm deeply weighed down by the feeling that I'm a fraud and that my clients would truly be better off without me.
Have you experienced episodes like this before, where you felt similarly overwhelmed and had thoughts of being a burden, or is this the first time you're experiencing these feelings?
No, this is the first time I have ever felt this way. I've never experienced an episode like this in the past, so it's all really new and terrifying to me.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'going through the motions' and how much these feelings and thoughts have impacted your daily functioning and ability to care for yourself?

By "going through the motions," I mean that things I used to love, like playing my guitar or hanging out with friends, now feel completely pointless and bring me no joy. It has gotten so bad that I've been calling in sick to work, letting my clinic documentation pile up, and ignoring basic chores like laundry and dishes because I just feel too overwhelmed to care for myself.

You mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, can you tell me if there are any activities that still bring you some sense of pleasure or if everything feels pointless to you right now?

Honestly, everything feels completely pointless right now and nothing brings me any pleasure. Even the things I used to love, like playing guitar or hanging out with friends, just feel like I'm going through the motions. I would honestly rather just sit in the dark staring at nothing than pretend I'm enjoying anything.
Have you had any thoughts of acting on these feelings of not wanting to wake up, such as making a plan to harm yourself or attempting to do so?

On my worst day, I actually wrote a note on my phone explaining why my clients would be better off without me and started looking up ways to kill myself. That really scared me, which is why I reached out to a coworker who helped me get this appointment.
Can you describe the difference between your worst days and the days that are slightly better, in terms of how overwhelming these thoughts and feelings of being a burden are to you?

On slightly better days, it's more of a passive feeling—I just replay my mistakes, feel like a fraud, and wish I wouldn't wake up in the morning. But on my worst day, the weight of being a burden became so overwhelming that I actually wrote a suicide note on my phone and looked up ways to end my life, which absolutely terrified me.

Given that this is your first episode of feeling this way, can you tell me if these intense feelings of being a burden and thoughts of not wanting to wake up have been constant over the past month, or have they varied in intensity?

They've been pretty constant for about a month now, and I catch myself thinking it would be a relief not to wake up pretty much every single night. But the intensity definitely peaked on that one really bad day when I actually wrote the note on my phone and looked up methods, which is what terrified me enough to get help.

Have you had any thoughts of acting on these feelings of not wanting to wake up since the day you wrote the note and looked up ways to harm yourself, or has the intensity of those thoughts decreased since then?

I haven't actively tried to make a plan or look up methods again since that day I wrote the note, which really scared me. But the passive thoughts of it being a relief if I just didn't wake up are still happening pretty much every night, and they're still really scary.

You've mentioned that everything feels pointless and nothing brings you pleasure right now, but can you think of any situation or event in the past month where you might have felt even a slight hint of pleasure or joy, no matter how small?

No, there hasn't been even a single moment of pleasure or joy this past month. Everything, including playing my guitar or hanging out with friends, feels completely pointless to me now. I would honestly rather just sit alone in the dark staring at nothing than force myself to pretend I'm enjoying anything.

You've mentioned that everything feels pointless and you've lost interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of any small, everyday things, like a good cup of coffee or a beautiful sunset, that might still bring you a tiny bit of comfort or relief, even if it's not exactly pleasure?

No, even those small everyday things don't bring me any comfort or relief right now. Everything truly feels completely pointless. I would honestly just prefer to sit in the dark staring at nothing rather than trying to find comfort in anything.

Can you describe how these feelings of being a burden and thoughts of not wanting to wake up have affected your daily functioning, such as your ability to work, eat, sleep, or maintain personal hygiene, over the past month?

My sleep is terrible because I lie awake for hours replaying my mistakes and wake up exhausted, and I have no appetite at all, so my clothes are getting loose. Just showering and getting to work feels like a marathon, so I've been calling in sick, letting my clinic notes pile up, and ignoring my friends. At home, I'm just too drained to function, so my laundry and dishes have been piling up for weeks.
Have you experienced any significant fluctuations in the intensity of your depressive symptoms over the past month, or have they remained relatively constant?
I'm not really sure about specific fluctuations, but it feels like it has been pretty constant. It has just been steadily getting worse over the past month without any real breaks.
Can you estimate how many days out of the past month you've felt these intense depressive symptoms, versus days where you might have felt slightly better or had a bit more energy?

It has been pretty much every single day for the past month. Since the stress at the clinic started, I haven't had any "good" days or days where I felt like I had more energy. It’s just been a constant, heavy weight on me every single day.

You've described a constant feeling of heaviness and depression over the past month, but can you tell me if there have been any days where you felt even slightly better, or has it been a completely unvarying experience?

It has felt pretty constant and unvarying, to be honest. I can't really recall any days over the past month where I felt genuinely better or noticed any lift in my mood. It's just been the same heavy weight day after day.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been constant over the past month, but can you tell me if you've experienced any periods, even brief, where your depressive symptoms seemed to worsen or improve slightly in response to anything, such as a change in your environment or support from others?

My symptoms generally feel worse at night when I'm alone in my apartment ruminating and scrolling, or after particularly stressful days at the clinic. I haven't really experienced any periods of improvement, though reaching out to my coworker was a crucial moment where I got scared enough to seek help.

Have you experienced any significant periods where your symptoms seemed to worsen or improve slightly in response to external factors, such as changes in your work environment or support from others, over the past month?

Yes, things definitely got worse in response to work stressors. It all started about a month ago after a series of really difficult cases and a tense argument with my supervisor. Recently, a particularly stressful workday triggered the worst of it, which is when I drafted that note on my phone and realized I had to reach out to my colleague for help.
Have you experienced any psychotic symptoms, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there, during this episode of feeling overwhelmed and thinking about not wanting to wake up?
No, I haven't experienced anything like that at all. I definitely haven't heard any voices or seen things that aren't actually there.
Have you experienced any other psychotic symptoms, such as delusions or disorganized thinking, during this episode?
No, I haven't experienced any delusions or disorganized thinking. My mind just feels incredibly slow and foggy, almost like it's full of mud, which makes it really hard to focus or think clearly.

You've described a range of depressive symptoms, but can you tell me if you've felt that these symptoms have been severe enough to significantly impair your ability to function in daily life, or have you been able to maintain some level of functioning despite these feelings?

Yes, my daily life has been severely impacted and I'm barely functioning. At work, I've been calling in sick, leaving early because running groups overwhelms me, and my documentation has piled up so much that my supervisor flagged it. Outside of work, I've been ignoring my friends' texts and letting chores like dishes and laundry pile up because I just can't handle anything.
Can you estimate how much of your daily life and activities you've had to stop or significantly reduce due to these feelings of depression and being a burden over the past month?

I've had to stop or scale back almost everything over the past month because I just can't deal with it. At work, I'm calling in sick or leaving early because running groups is too overwhelming, and my clinic documentation is completely piling up. Outside of that, I'm ignoring texts from my friends and letting basic chores like dishes and laundry pile up at home.
Can you rate the overall impact of your symptoms on your daily life, from 1 to 10, where 1 is minimal impact and 10 is complete inability to function?

I would rate it as an 8 or 9 out of 10 because it has severely disrupted my ability to function. At work, I'm constantly calling in sick, falling behind on my documentation, and getting flagged by my supervisor, while at home I'm too overwhelmed to do basic chores like laundry and dishes or even reply to my friends.

Can you tell me if there are any specific days or periods over the past month where you felt like you were at your absolute lowest point, or if the feelings of depression and being a burden have been at a consistently high level throughout?

While the heavy feeling and sense of being a burden have been consistently weighing me down for about a month, my absolute lowest point was on a particularly stressful day at the clinic. That was when I actually wrote a suicide note on my phone and started looking up ways to end my life. It terrified me so much that I immediately reached out to my coworker for help.
Can you clarify if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt like you were slightly better or if your symptoms have remained at the same severe level throughout the past month?

No, there haven't been any periods where I felt better or got a break from this. Ever since those difficult cases and the argument with my supervisor, the heavy feelings have been completely constant. It has just been a steady, severe weight on me for the entire month.

You've mentioned having suicidal thoughts and writing a note, but can you tell me if you've had any thoughts of acting on those feelings since the day you wrote the note, or have those thoughts remained passive?

Since that scary day when I wrote the note and looked up methods, the thoughts have gone back to being passive, and I haven't made any plans or taken any active steps since. I still catch myself thinking every night that it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up, but writing that note really terrified me, which is why I reached out to my coworker.
Have you had any thoughts of self-harm or suicidal ideation in the past few days, or have those thoughts decreased in frequency or intensity since you first sought help?

Yes, those thoughts are still very intense and haven't really decreased, since I'm only just now seeking help. Pretty much every night I still find myself thinking it would be a relief if I didn't wake up. It keeps bringing me back to my worst day recently, when I actually wrote that suicide note on my phone and looked up ways to kill myself, which terrified me enough to reach out to my coworker.
Have you experienced any variation in the frequency or intensity of your suicidal thoughts over the past few days, or have they remained relatively consistent?

They've been pretty consistent over the past few days, and I still catch myself thinking it would be a relief if I just didn't wake up every single night. While that moment when I wrote the note on my phone was the absolute peak of intensity, the general feeling of wanting to disappear has stayed constant. It just doesn't seem to go away.
Have you experienced any significant increase or decrease in the frequency of your suicidal thoughts since you first started experiencing them about a month ago?

They have definitely become more frequent and severe, to the point where I have those thoughts pretty much every night now. On my worst day, it escalated to me actually writing a suicide note on my phone and looking up ways to end my life. That really scared me and is what finally led me to reach out to my coworker for help.
Have you experienced any significant increase in the intensity of your suicidal thoughts since you first sought help, or have they remained relatively consistent?

Since reaching out, they haven't increased beyond that peak on my worst day when I wrote the note and looked up methods, which is what scared me into getting help. The thoughts of wishing I wouldn't wake up are still happening pretty much every night and remain really scary, but I haven't taken any active steps like writing more notes since then.
